summary: Torn session tails are recoverable: open_existing_writable (and thus open_in_workspace / resume) quarantines a newline-less unparsable final line to <file>.torn (0600, appended, fsynced) under the append lock and truncates to the last complete record; any other corruption still rejects. session_catalog skips dirty journals (new session_catalog_with_skipped returns SkippedSession warnings) and keeps torn-tail-only journals, so one corrupt file no longer breaks listing/resume-last. append_encoded writes via write_or_rollback, truncating to observed_bytes on write/flush/sync failure so the writer never goes stale. New session files (create_fresh and writable open that creates the file) fsync the parent directory.
diff_stat: src/session.rs | 254 +++-, tests/session_torn_tail.rs | 142 +++ (code: 2 files changed, 379 insertions(+), 17 deletions(-)) + handoff json
commands_run: cargo test --no-fail-fast --test core_session --test session_new --test session_recovery --test stage1_session_tree --test resume_compact_owner --test headless_protocol --test session_torn_tail --test session_cli

validation_result.clippy: pass (default and --all-features; only pre-existing vendored crossterm warning)
validation_result.torn_tail_open_in_workspace_append: pass: open_in_workspace + append_turn succeed; .torn holds fragment, mode 0600; file = clean prefix + new turn
validation_result.corrupt_sibling_resume_last: pass: catalog lists 1 entry + 1 skipped; resume_last_session and lifecycle ResumeLast return the good session
validation_result.failed_write_rollback_unit: pass: partial write then error truncates to observed_bytes; later append succeeds and journal reopens clean
validation_result.session_suites: pass: headless_protocol 45, resume_compact_owner 6, session_cli 5, session_new 14, session_recovery 45, session_torn_tail 4, stage1_session_tree 13(+1 ignored); core_session 40/41 in parallel, 41/41 with --test-threads=1

notes: core_session::user_shell_preserves_nonzero_signal_and_cancellation_evidence is timing-based (<2s cancel bound) and flaked under parallel load; passes alone and with --test-threads=1. SessionLifecycleReceipt::Catalog is unchanged (headless.rs not owned), so skipped-session warnings are exposed via session_catalog_with_skipped for a later owner to surface. .torn is appended (not overwritten) so repeated crashes keep earlier fragments. Torn-tail repair requires a valid header and that the only warning is a JSON parse failure on the newline-less final line.
